requested review from @alex

This is a well-scoped CI maintenance change and the version bumps (kind, kubectl, docker, alpine, helm-unittest) and URL fixes (dl.k8s.io, docker:-cli, pinned DESIRED_VERSION for get-helm-3) all look correct and consistent with the stated rationale. I flagged one concern worth checking before merge: the new default image (`alpine/helm:${HELM_VERSION}`) replaces an old, pre-PEP668 Alpine base for jobs that still do a bare `pip install awscli` (namely `release beta`), which could start failing with an externally-managed-environment error depending on the Alpine version baked into that image — this job isn't exercised by this MR's own pipeline run since it only fires on `main`. I also noted, at low confidence, the general supply-chain tradeoff of depending on an unofficial `alpine/helm` image instead of a GitLab-maintained one. Everything else — the `entrypoint: [""]` override, the parameterized `DOCKER_VERSION`/`KUBECTL_VERSION`/`KIND_VERSION`/`HELM_VERSION` variables, and the integration test's `kubectl`/`helm` install steps — checks out against the affected scripts and jobs.

1 finding (1 major) across 1 file:

**Major**
- ci-image-regression: `.gitlab-ci.yml:74`

On the `alpine/helm` image: `gitlab-build-images` has no Helm-only image newer than `gitlab-charts-build-base-helm-3.9`, and its tags are not version-shaped, so they cannot be kept current by an update bot. `alpine/helm` is the image published by the alpine-docker organisation and is what `charts/gitlab` style tooling and many Helm projects use; its tag follows the Helm version, which is what `HELM_VERSION` tracks. If maintainers prefer a GitLab-maintained image, I am happy to switch, the only requirement for the follow-up (#603) is a version-shaped tag.

Switching the default image from the old gitlab-build-images Helm 3.7 image to `alpine/helm:${HELM_VERSION}` also changes the base Alpine version under `release beta`, which still runs `apk add --no-cache py-pip` followed by `pip install awscli` without overriding `image:`. Recent Alpine releases (3.19+) ship pip with PEP 668 enforced, so a bare `pip install` fails with an externally-managed-environment error unless `--break-system-packages` (or a venv) is used. The old build-base-helm-3.7 image predates that restriction, so this job may have worked by accident until now. Has this been verified against the actual Alpine version baked into `alpine/helm:3.22.1`, since `release beta` only runs on pushes to main and wouldn't be caught by this MR's own pipeline?

Good catch, confirmed. `alpine/helm:3.22.1` is based on Alpine 3.24.2, and in that image `apk add py-pip && pip install awscli` fails with `error: externally-managed-environment`.

Fixed in cd2d128 by installing the `aws-cli` package from the Alpine community repository instead of pip (`apk add --no-cache aws-cli`). Verified in the same image: `aws --version` reports `aws-cli/2.34.63`. The `aws s3 cp` / `aws s3 sync --acl public-read` invocations used by the job are unchanged between awscli v1 and v2. The `sed -r` substitutions of the job also work on this image.

`release beta` still only runs on `main`, so the end-to-end run can only be confirmed after merge.

This is a re-review focused on the one line added since my last pass: `release beta` now runs `apk add --no-cache aws-cli` instead of `apk add --no-cache py-pip` + `pip install awscli`.

- Confirmed this directly fixes the PEP 668 externally-managed-environment failure I flagged previously, since the job runs under the new `alpine/helm` (Alpine 3.24) base image with no per-job image override.
- The author verified in commit cd2d1286 that `aws --version` reports `aws-cli/2.34.63` in that image, and that the `aws s3 cp` / `aws s3 sync --acl public-read` calls used later in the job are unaffected by the v1→v2 awscli switch.
- Checked the rest of the job's script (git config, sed substitutions, `helm package`, `helm repo index`) for any interaction with the aws-cli change; none found — these steps are unaffected.
- No new correctness, security, or regression issues found in this change.

Both previous discussion threads are addressed: the PEP 668 / pip install issue is fixed, and the general alpine/helm-image supply-chain question was explained by the author with no code change needed.
